name: Build orchestrator
author: Brett
description: Breaks every build into small steps (10 min or less; checkpoints inside one session, each committed and ticked as it finishes), each pinned to Fable or Opus, and runs the build pipeline (Brett, Nov 8 2026): every build gets an id and a Claude split (Fable only where needed) and sits in Pending; Brett moves it to the Queue; the dispatcher (pipeline.mjs on the VPS, every minute) watches the Claude accounts (which have Fable, parallel per account) and the agent slots and, when a slot is free, starts a headless session for the next Queue build on an account that runs its next phase's model. The only place that browses and manages builds (Brett, Nov 10 2026; the Build manager is retired): tabs Pending, Queue (each build's steps, planned model and account), Active, Incomplete, Complete, Errors, Archive (every completed and archived build), Deleted (soft-deleted builds kept forever, restorable), then Accounts (health every 5 minutes: sign-in, credits, Fable), All builds, Approvals and Rules. When a build's turn comes the dispatcher makes the final account pick, subscriptions first (in Brett's order), then any API account, moving on until one accepts, and records which account took it. Tracker is the one builds store, _claude/builds/store.json, so any session or account continues the build (orchestrator.mjs next | brief | act; pipeline.mjs status | queue | unqueue | hold | release | archive | unarchive | delete | restore | split | tick).

items.title: Build priorities
items.description: Every build's priority tag (Urgent, High, Normal, Low = P0-P3) and how many things wait on it.

items.title: What's waiting on a build
items.description: A build's priority and everything waiting for it: builds behind it in the agent queue, builds that depend on it, PRs stacked on it or behind it in the merge queue, UI Review items, linked plans. Say 'what's waiting on skins'.
items.output: { id, title, priority, label, waiting: [{ kind, id, title, why }] }

items.title: Headless runs and start tokens
items.description: A build's headless runs: start tokens (the context of the first request), cost, brief only or full chain, tools and MCP servers loaded. Say 'what did skins start with'.
items.output: { build, runs: [{ session, briefOnly, startTokens, startCostUsd, costUsd, at }] }

items.title: Set build priority
items.description: Set the priority of one or more builds: 'make banner widgets urgent'. Higher priority starts first in the agent queue and lands first in the merge queue; Brett's manual moves still win.

priority.description: urgent, high, normal, low or P0-P3

items.title: What Brett said
items.description: The verbatim words Brett used to start a build (build-origin@1): when, where, who launched it, the brief and later addenda.

items.title: Record what Brett said
items.description: Record Brett's verbatim words on a build that has none (backfilled ones give way); his words are never replaced: use origin-addendum for a later change.

said.description: Brett's exact words, verbatim and unedited (never a paraphrase)

items.title: Add what Brett said later
items.description: Append a later change Brett asked for (verbatim) to a build's origin.

said.description: Brett's exact words, verbatim and unedited (never a paraphrase)

items.title: Builds table (by status)
items.description: Pipeline 2.0's one builds table, driven only by status: every build with its status (pending, splitting, pulling main, assigning models, ready, sending, building, build complete, merging to one PR, PR pulling main, running CI, merging into main, landed, or failed with its attempt), steps done of total, model, account, slot, PR and when it entered its status. queue=true is the merge queue (merging-pr through merging-main); landed=true includes landed builds. Read from the builds store on Postgres. Say 'what's building', 'what's in the merge queue'.
items.output: { rev, updatedAt, profile, rows: [{ id, title, status, attempt, done, total, model, account, slot, prNumber, at, by, steps: [{ id, title, status, attempt, model, account, slot, prNumber, at, by }] }] } or { unchanged, rev } with since=<rev>

items.title: Pipeline status
items.description: The build pipeline: what is Pending, in the Queue and Building, every Claude account (Fable yes or no, how many run on it), the agent slots, and what the dispatcher's next tick will start or why it waits. Say 'what's in the queue' or 'is anything building'.
items.output: { table: { pending, queued, building } (rows carry requeue: { reason, phase, next, at } when back in the Queue after a finished phase, stuck: { phase, next, why } when parked in Pending by mistake), accounts, accountsFrom: { source, at, ageMin, why }, slots, plan: { launches, waits, idle }, state: { selfCheck, selfCheckRequested, … } }

items.title: Dispatcher self-check
items.description: Ask the dispatcher to check every Claude account one by one (signed in, limited, API key saved and not rejected, free slots), release slots and builds held by sessions that ended, and rebuild its account list. Runs on the VPS on the next tick (within a minute); the result shows on the Pipeline tab and in pipeline status (state.selfCheck), and AmberX hears when it fixed something or found an account it can't use. Say 'check the build accounts' or 'why is nothing building'.

reason.description: Why the check was asked for

items.output: { ran: false, requested, last: { at, line, fixes, problems, findings } }

items.title: Requeue builds parked after a phase
items.description: Find Pending builds whose last session finished its phase with steps left (parked by the old exit rule, so the next phase never started) and, with apply, move them back to the Queue at their place so the dispatcher starts the next phase. Without apply it only lists them. Say 'requeue the stuck builds' or 'which builds are stuck after a phase'.

apply.description: Move them (true) or only list them (false, the default)

items.output: { apply, found: [{ id, phase, next, why }], moved: [id] }

items.title: A build's launches and bounces
items.description: What the dispatcher knows about a build's launches: runs, crashes, the launch-retry record (lastLaunchError, retries, retryAt, gaveUp after 3 launch crashes in a row) and the last land-clash bounce (bounceReason, the merge-main step it added). Say 'why won't skins start' or 'did skins crash at launch'.
items.output: { id, status, runs, crashes, lastRun, launchRetry, lastLaunchError, retries, retryAt, gaveUp, bounce, bounceReason }

items.title: Requeue a build that crashed at launch
items.description: Put a build that crashed at launch (E2BIG, a launcher error, a session that died before its first output) back in the Queue now, with its launch retries reset, including one that stopped retrying by itself. Say 'requeue skins' or 'try starting skins again'.

items.title: Bounce a clashing build back to the Queue
items.description: A build with every step done whose branch clashes with main gets one Opus step 'Merge main into <branch> and resolve conflicts in <files>' and goes back to the Queue so the dispatcher runs it. Without files the server works the clash out with git; the same clash never adds a second step. The dispatcher does this by itself when the lander reports a conflict. Say 'phone connect clashes with main, send it back'.

files.description: Optional: the conflicting files (default: worked out by git merge-tree)

head.description: Optional: the branch head the clash is on

items.output: { id, bounced: { id, step, text, status } | null, files, head, clash? }

items.title: Collapse repeated build steps
items.description: Collapse steps a build has more than once (a done copy wins, order of first appearance), one journal revision per build. Without apply it only counts them. Every store write already refuses repeats; this cleans what was stored before. Say 'dedupe the build steps' or 'how many repeated steps are there'.

apply.description: Write it (true) or only count (false, the default)

items.output: { apply, builds: [{ id, before, after, renamed }], total: { before, after } }

items.title: Orchestrator tab
items.description: One of the orchestrator's tabs: pending, queue, active, incomplete, complete, errors, archive (every completed and archived build) or deleted (soft-deleted builds, kept forever), with each build's steps, planned model and account, the account that took it, whether it is on hold and the actions it offers. Say 'what's in the queue', 'show the archive' or 'show deleted builds'.
items.output: { tab, rows: [{ id, title, status, held, actions, deleted, deletedAt, steps, stepList, pipeline: { planned, account, pickedAt, tried, heldAt, heldBy, heldWhy } }] }

items.title: Claude account health
items.description: The last account health sweep (every 5 minutes, headless, never touches a build): per account, can sign in, has credits, accepts Fable. Say 'are the accounts healthy'.
items.output: { health: { at, line, problems, accounts: [{ name, kind, signedIn, credits, fable, error }] }, every }

items.title: Check the Claude accounts now
items.description: Run the account health sweep now (the dispatcher starts it within a minute, in the background). Say 'check the accounts now'.

items.title: Queue a build
items.description: Move a Pending build to the Queue: the dispatcher starts it when a slot and an account for its model are free. Say 'queue the icon browser build'.

items.title: Take a build out of the Queue
items.description: Move a queued build back to Pending before it starts.

items.title: Emergency builds
items.description: The builds Brett sent to emergency (they skip the line, build in the 2 emergency slots and land first), each with its status and whether its slot grant is on file.
items.output: { builds: [{ id, title, status, emergency: { at, by }, granted }], canSend }

items.title: Send a build to emergency
items.description: Brett only, from his own signed-in console session: the console token (this command through REST, MCP, the CLI or voice) is refused with 403. Tags a Pipeline 2.0 build as emergency: it skips the one-active-build line, builds in the emergency slot pool and lands first.

items.title: Make an emergency build ordinary again
items.description: Removes the emergency tag and the emergency slot grant. Sessions already running finish; the build waits its turn like any other.

items.title: Hold, archive, delete or restore builds
items.description: Act on one build or many at once (bulk): unqueue (Queue back to Pending), hold (stays in the Queue, the dispatcher skips it until released), release, archive, unarchive, delete (soft delete: kept in the builds store forever, Deleted tab) or restore. Builds with a live session are refused; the rest still go. Say 'hold the icon browser build', 'archive these builds' or 'restore the deleted toast build'.

why.description: Why (kept in the build notes; hold and delete)

items.output: { action, done: [{ id, status, tab }], refused: [{ id, error }] }

items.title: Split a build into steps
items.description: Ask the orchestrator to split (or re-split) a build into steps of 10 minutes or less, Fable only where needed; done by the dispatcher within a minute.

items.title: Ask for a build
items.description: File a build with the orchestrator and put it in the Queue: the orchestrator is the only thing that starts builds; it assigns the id, splits it and the dispatcher launches it on the right account and model. Say 'build me …'.

queue.description: Straight to the Queue (default true); false = Pending

items.title: Route a build to API or subscriptions
items.description: Where one build may run: api (API-key accounts only, billed per token under their daily and weekly caps; Brett's own click), subscription (never an API account) or auto (subscriptions, API only by the overflow rule).

items.title: Pipeline settings
items.description: The dispatcher's settings, including the API overflow rule (apiOverflow) and which API accounts it may use.

items.title: Change pipeline settings
items.description: Change dispatcher settings. apiOverflow = when every subscription account is full or out, send builds to an API-key account (off by default; turning it on is Brett's own click, anyone may turn it off).

items.title: Fill every slot: slots and ready steps
items.description: Which build and step runs in each agent slot (or free), the ready steps of running builds, what the next dispatcher round would start (dry run, with why the rest waits) and the fill settings; with build, that build's steps and their dependency state (done, running in slot N, ready, waiting on). Say 'what's in the slots' or 'what runs in parallel'.

build.description: Build id (adds its steps and their dependency state)

items.output: { settings: { fillSlots, autoQueuePending, maxParallelPerBuild }, slots: { cap, used, free, rows: [{ n, build, step, state, session }] }, ready, builds: [{ id, parallel, cap }], plan: { launches, waits, free, blocked }, build?: { steps: [{ id, state, dependsOn, waitingOn, runningIn }] } }

items.title: Fill the slots now
items.description: Run one dispatcher round now: ready parallel steps start in the free slots (and Queue builds, and Pending ones when auto-queue is on). On the VPS it runs at once; from the console it is filed and runs within a minute. Say 'fill the slots'.
items.output: { ran, requested?, launched, fill: { launched, ended, autoQueued, plan } }

items.title: Set a step's dependencies
items.description: Set which steps of the build one step waits for: a list of step ids ([] = independent, it may run in parallel as soon as the build runs) or null = sequential (it waits for the step before it). Unknown ids, the step itself and cycles are refused. Say 'step 4 of the icon build only needs step 1'.

dependsOn.description: Step ids it waits for; [] = independent; null = sequential

items.title: Fill every slot settings
items.description: Fill every slot (run independent steps in parallel; anyone may switch it off, only Brett on), max parallel steps per build (1-12; only Brett raises it) and auto-queue pending builds (owner-only: refused unless Brett's own click). Say 'turn off fill every slot' or 'one parallel step per build'.

items.title: Build groups
items.description: Every custom group on the builds board of the active project: name, colour, tab, sort, filter, smart rule, its builds sorted by state (partial, pending, queued, running, failed, done, landed) and the count per state, plus the Pending builds in no group. Say 'what's in my console app group'.
items.output: { profile, groups: [{ id, name, color, tab, sort, filter, rule, counts, total, rows, tabRows }], loose }

items.title: Custom build tabs
items.description: The groups pinned as tabs next to Pending, Queue, Active … and the builds each tab shows (a custom Pending tab is a group pinned next to Pending). Deep link: build-orchestrator.tab:group:<id>.
items.output: { tabs: [{ id: 'group:<id>', group, label, stage, color, count, rows }] }

items.title: One build group
items.description: One group by id or name with its builds sorted the group's way and the count per state.

items.title: Create, edit, reorder, delete or fill a build group
items.description: op=create {name, color?, tab?, sort?, filter?, rule?, builds?} makes a group ('make a group called UI with its own pending tab'); op=update {group, name?, color?, tab?, sort?, filter?, rule?} renames, recolours, pins it as a tab (tab = pending, queue, active, incomplete, complete, errors, archive, all or none), changes the sort or the states shown, or sets a smart rule (rule = {titleContains, behindMoreThan, filedWithinDays, states, priorities}; null clears it); op=move {group, to: index|up|down|first|last}; op=delete {group} (its builds stay); op=assign {groups, builds, mode: add|remove|set} puts builds in one or several groups ('put skins and banner widgets in Urgent'). Saved per project.

group.description: Group id or name (update, move, delete)

filter.description: States shown: partial, pending, queued, running, failed, done, landed (empty = all)

to.description: move: index, up, down, first or last

items.title: Run an action on a whole build group
items.description: queue = every Pending build of the group goes to the Queue; land = every Done build goes first in the merge queue (tagged Urgent); archive = every build without a live session goes to the Archive; priority = every build gets the priority. Say 'queue all of console app', 'make the UI group urgent'.

priority.description: urgent, high, normal, low or P0-P3 (action priority)

items.output: { group, action, done: [id], refused: [{ id, error }], skipped: [{ id, state }] }

items.title: A build's attempts
items.description: done-means-merged@1: every try at getting a build past a failure (crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push, a stall, a fall back to Pending) with its strategy, model, account and result; the open failure, the merge + CI + verify evidence, the escalation and what the retry ladder tries next. Say 'what's wrong with skins' or 'why did skins stop'.
items.output: { id, status, attempts: [{ n, kind, strategy, fixStrategy, model, account, result, startedAt, endedAt, note }], failure, landed, escalation, ladder, next }

items.title: Retry a build
items.description: Retry a fixing or escalated build: the ladder starts over for its failure (the attempts so far stay in the log), the next tick relaunches it, or at once on the strategy given (never above the step's pinned model). A Pipeline 2.0 build that failed (given up at attempt 5 included): the build and its failed steps go forward again from the status they failed at with their attempt counts reset, and the next pass carries on; a strategy is not used. Say 'retry skins' or 'retry skins in a fresh session'.

strategy.description: Optional: the rung to run now

items.title: Build watchdog status
items.description: The one build watchdog and every watch it runs (build sessions, stuck statuses, left-over rows): on or off, the cron, the last pass and how long ago, each watch's last run, what it caught and its last error, and the newest catches. Say 'what did the watchdog catch' or 'is the watchdog running'.
items.output: watchdogs-status@1 { enabled, alerts, cron, lastPass, ageMin, stale, watches[], caught[], gaveUp[] }

items.title: What the watchdog caught
items.description: Everything the build watchdog caught, newest first: the watch, the build, the status it stood in, the cause, the action taken (retry, requeue, record-merge, land, fail, ladder rung, escalate, complete, remove), whether it worked and whether the phone was told. Filter by watch (sessions, stale, rows) or build.

items.title: Dry-run the build watchdog
items.description: What each watch would catch right now and what it would do about it, changing nothing. From the console container it answers with what the VPS's last pass saw.

watch.description: only this watch: sessions, stale or rows

items.title: Run the build watchdog now
items.description: One watchdog pass now, for every watch or one, optionally for one build: stuck sessions recovered, builds standing in landing or fixing pushed to the next action on their ladder, left-over rows cleaned. From the console the VPS runs it within a minute.

watch.description: only this watch: sessions, stale or rows

items.output: watchdogs-pass@1 { ran[], notRun[], catches[], alerts } or { requested: true }

items.title: Build watchdog settings
items.description: Every watchdog setting in one flat map with its type, range and title: enabled (the master switch), alerts (batch, each, off), and each watch's own under <watch>.<key>, e.g. sessions.maxRetries, stale.limit.fixing, stale.maxLaunchPerPass, rows.intervalMin.

items.title: Change build watchdog settings
items.description: Change any watchdog setting: switch the watchdog or one watch on or off (enabled, stale.enabled), thresholds (stale.limit.landing, stale.limit.fixing, sessions.staleMin), caps (stale.maxLaunchPerPass, sessions.maxRetries), intervals and alerts. Send {key: value}; each value is checked and unknown keys are refused.

items.title: Stale-row watchdog status
items.description: The VPS stale-row watchdog: its settings (on/off, every how many minutes, dry run only, which lists it watches, notify), the last run (rows read, found, cleaned, GitHub calls), the last runs and the newest cleanup log records. Say 'what did the watchdog clean'.

log.description: how many cleanup log records to include (default 20)

items.output: { settings, schema, last, lastOk, running, runs, log }

items.title: Run the stale-row watchdog now
items.description: Run the watchdog now: rows on Pending, Queue, Building, the merge queue and UI Review whose PR merged are completed, rows whose PR closed or whose build died are removed; running builds are never touched. Logged, noted on the builds, one FYI to AmberX. force=true runs even when it is off.

force.description: run even when the watchdog is switched off

items.title: Dry-run the stale-row watchdog
items.description: What the watchdog would clean right now and why, changing nothing.
items.output: watchdog-run@1 { dry: true, rows, planned, changes[] }

items.title: Watchdog cleanup log
items.description: Every row the watchdog completed or removed (stale-row-log@1), newest first, with the reason and evidence. Filter by list kind, action or build.

items.title: Change watchdog settings
items.description: Change the stale-row watchdog's settings: enabled (on/off), intervalMin (1-120), dryRun, tables.builds / tables.merge-queue / tables.ui-review (which lists it watches), notify (the FYI to AmberX).

items.title: Build watchdog status
items.description: The build watchdog: on or off, its cron, the last pass and how long ago (stale after 3 min), what the VPS saw for every build marked running (pid, tmux, heartbeat, exit), recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, told the phone) and builds it gave up on. Say 'watchdog status'.
items.output: watchdog-status@1 { settings, cron, lastPass, ageMin, stale, lastScan, recent, gaveUp }

items.title: Watchdog dry run
items.description: Every build marked running with what the probe saw, why it is stuck (killed 143, failed 1, OOM 137, usage limit, dead login, tmux or claude gone, stale heartbeat) and what the watchdog would do. Changes nothing.
items.output: { source, at, builds: [{ id, probe, cause, stuck, action, attempt, note }], stuck }

items.title: Run the watchdog now
items.description: One watchdog pass now: stuck builds reset, requeued or retried (another account on a usage limit), slots released and refilled, a phone FYI per fix. From the console the VPS runs it within a minute. Say 'run the watchdog'.

items.title: Requeue builds the watchdog gave up on
items.description: Fix (requeue): builds the watchdog gave up on (past Max retries, or every account tried) go back to the Queue with a fresh retry count. No builds = all of them.

items.title: Watchdog settings
items.description: The Watchdog settings: enabled, intervalMin, staleMin, graceMin, maxRetries, retryOtherAccount, fyi (batch | each), cooldownMin.

items.title: Change the watchdog settings
items.description: Change any Watchdog setting: switch it on or off, the interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, one phone FYI per fix or batched. Say 'set watchdog max retries to 5'.

items.title: A build's recoveries
items.description: Every time the watchdog reset, requeued or retried a build: when, the cause, the action, the attempt, whether the phone was told.
